title: Trump announces members of 'Super Intelligence Force' to coordinate AI policy
key_facts: President Trump announced an AI task force on Sunday 4 Oct, called the Super Intelligence Force, and named National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton to lead it.
Other members include FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson and Defense Undersecretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael.
Trump said the group reports to him and to chief of staff Susie Wiles.

Per Trump's Truth Social post, it will coordinate federal engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and 'Super Intelligence Companies'.
It follows a Tuesday meeting with tech leaders including Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Tesla's Elon Musk and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, and a 'White House Accord on Super Intelligence'.
Trump has said he will not regulate the industry and described the accord as 'tremendous self-regulation'.
NBC reported Friday that Trump was expected to name Clayton AI czar; David Sacks left that role when his term as a special government employee expired.
quote_evidence: President Donald Trump announced the formation of an artificial intelligence task force Sunday, naming National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton to lead it.
The task force, Trump said, will report to him and to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
Last week, after the summit, Trump said the leaders had reached what appeared to be a nonbinding agreement of "tremendous self-regulation."
why_it_matters_hint: Sets up a White House body to coordinate AI policy while the administration says it will rely on voluntary industry commitments.
